newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives say opponents risk dismembering UK.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives say opponents risk dismembering UK.

text.p: Britain's two main opposition parties were accused by Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth on Tuesday of being ready to risk the break-up of Britain with their plans to devolve power to Scotland and Wales.

"Labour and their Liberal Democrat satellites are so intent on gerrymandering our constitution that they are actually prepared to risk the dismemberment of the United Kingdom," Forsyth told the ruling Conservative Party annual conference.
"There is no such thing as Scottish devolution -- there is only British dissolution," Forsyth, widely tipped as a possible compromise candidate to succeed John Major as party leader, added.

He attacked Labour for having changed its policy on a Scottish assembly four times, saying the reason was that the scheme contained internal contradictions which were impossible to reconcile short of Scottish independence.
"There could only be one eventual resolution of the intolerable tensions inherent in Labour's scheme -- the departure of Scotland from the United Kingdom," Forsyth said.
